output.brief: Don't send the breach notice. The rise in Corvane's mishandled bags comes from bag tags that the automatic readers can't read, not from Tessaly's handling. Tags printed on the new Fennick stock since 1 September fail to read 11.8% of the time, against 1.5% on the old Brackwater stock. Counters and kiosks fail at about the same rate. On 14–16 October, counters that used Brackwater stock from stores went back to 1.6%. Unreadable bags go to the manual encode desk. Encode wait times rose from 7 to 33 minutes. About 91% of the late bags reached the lateral after it closed. Pelion uses the same Tessaly crew pool and stayed flat at about 3.7. Corvane bags that read automatically also stayed flat. The airport's readers look fine. The new evening flights don't explain the rise. I'm fairly confident (about 85%) in this. What I haven't established is whether the Fennick stock is defective or just mismatched to the printers' heat settings. Next steps: return to Brackwater stock now, since about five weeks is in stores and the contract runs to 31 Dec. Then test the Fennick stock and the printer settings, and check the encode desk staffing. Hold off on a claim against Fennick until the test result is in. Don't withhold Tessaly's fee.
